newsitem.title: USA: Nichols' jurors summoned and ensured of privacy.
newsitem.headline: Nichols' jurors summoned and ensured of privacy.

text.p: Jury summonses for the trial of Oklahoma City bombing defendant Terry Nichols were mailed Thursday to 1,000 Coloradans, court officials said.
The potential jurors were told to immediately begin avoiding news accounts of the case and that their privacy will be protected. They will not be sequestered.
The two-page jury notice from U.S. District Court Judge Richard Matsch was almost identical to the one sent in February to the jury pool for the trial of co-defendant Timothy McVeigh.
In June, jurors convicted McVeigh of the April 19, 1995 bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City that killed 168 people. He was sentenced to die.
Nichols' trial is to begin Sept. 29 with jury selection.

Potential jurors in September will fill out an extensive, confidential questionnaire about their knowledge of the case and other issues that Matsch, prosecutors and defence attorneys will use for screening.

In the notice, Matsch directed the potential jurors to immediately begin avoiding news accounts, conversations and anything else that "may interfere with your ability to be open-minded and decide this case according to the law and evidence."
